flagship.headline: Elvis Presley releases Return to Sender
flagship.summary_line_1: RCA Victor released Elvis Presley's Return to Sender, a rock and roll single written by Otis Blackwell and Winfield Scott and featured in his film Girls! Girls! Girls!.
flagship.summary_line_2: The single sold more than a million copies, became that year's UK Christmas number one, and reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100.

events.headline: The Beatles begin recording Hello, Goodbye
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles gathered at Studio Two, EMI Studios, from 10pm to 2:30am to lay down the basic track for Paul McCartney's Hello, Goodbye, then known by the working title Hello Hello.
events.summary_line_2: Producer George Martin and engineers Geoff Emerick and Ken Scott oversaw 14 takes of the rhythm track, the start of sessions that produced the group's next international No. 1 single.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones play two shows at the Gaumont Theatre in Ipswich
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones performed two houses at the Gaumont Theatre in Ipswich, with support from Ike & Tina Turner and the Yardbirds on their 1966 British tour.
events.summary_line_2: The bill paired the Stones with two acts near the height of their own powers, part of a tour that closed out the band's era of small theatre package shows before stadiums took over.

events.headline: John Coltrane performs A Love Supreme live in Seattle
events.summary_line_1: John Coltrane led an expanded group, his classic quartet plus Pharoah Sanders in his first gig with the band, through a full live performance of A Love Supreme at The Penthouse jazz club in Seattle.
events.summary_line_2: Recorded by local saxophonist Joe Brazil and not discovered until years after his death, the tapes surfaced in 2021 as A Love Supreme: Live in Seattle, one of only two known full live performances of Coltrane's landmark suite.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones play two shows at Wigan's ABC Cinema
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones performed at 6:20 and 8:35pm at the ABC Cinema in Wigan, the night after their shows in Chester, deep into their second British tour of the year.
events.summary_line_2: The dates came months after (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction had turned the band into Britain's biggest live draw, packing theatres night after night.

events.headline: The Beatles rehearse for the US show Shindig!
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles gathered at Granville Studio in Fulham Broadway to rehearse three songs, Kansas City, I'm a Loser and Boys, for a British-made segment of the American TV show Shindig!, produced by Jack Good.
events.summary_line_2: The rehearsal set up a live taping in front of fans the very next day, giving American viewers a fresh look at the band just months after Beatlemania first hit the United States.

events.headline: Andrew Oldham Orchestra & Chorus release 16 Hip Hits
events.summary_line_1: Decca's budget Ace of Clubs label issued 16 Hip Hits by the Andrew Oldham Orchestra & Chorus, an album of orchestral covers of current hits arranged by Rolling Stones manager Andrew Loog Oldham.
events.summary_line_2: Rolling Stones guitarist Keith Richards played uncredited guitar on several tracks, including a version of Needles and Pins, blurring the line between the Stones' rock and roll and Oldham's pop orchestrations.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones play two 10-minute sets at Edmonton's Regal Theatre
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones performed two brief sets at the Regal Theatre in Edmonton, north London, opening for Bo Diddley and the Everly Brothers on their first UK package tour.
events.summary_line_2: Paid about £20 a show as a band, the dates were a grueling proving ground for the Rolling Stones just weeks before their first hit single, Come On, cracked the UK charts.

events.summary_line_2: The single sold more than a million copies, became that year's UK Christmas number one, and reached No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100.

events.headline: The McGuire Sisters sing Kids on The Ed Sullivan Show
events.summary_line_1: The McGuire Sisters, joined by the young singing trio the Kane Triplets, performed Kids from the Broadway hit Bye Bye Birdie on CBS's The Ed Sullivan Show.
events.summary_line_2: The appearance carried the sweet vocal-group harmonies that had defined the sisters' fifties hits into primetime television just as rock and roll began reshaping the pop charts.
